name: acute coronary syndrome overview
title: Acute coronary syndrome decision chart: the first ECG splits ST-elevation MI (reperfuse now: primary PCI, else fibrinolysis) from no ST elevation, where troponin splits NSTEMI from unstable angina (antithrombotics, then angiography); a second band sorts complications after the MI (right ventricular infarction, pump failure or rupture, arrhythmia and block, post-MI pericarditis) with presentation, investigations and treatment

root.title: Suspected acute coronary syndrome (ACS): stabilize, ASA, 12-lead ECG within 10 MINUTES
lines: > 15–30 min crushing retrosternal pain to the arm or jaw, sweating; atypical or silent in women, the elderly, diabetics
ASA 162–325 mg chewed, NOT if aortic dissection is possible (arm blood pressures differ > 20 mmHg)
AFTER every myocardial infarction (MI): ASA for life + 2nd antiplatelet 12 months; rehab + other drugs: see the SECONDARY PREVENTION chart

groups.title: ST ELEVATION
lines: ≥ 1 mm in 2 contiguous leads (2 mm in V2–V3) or NEW left bundle branch block

groups.title: NO ST elevation
lines: ST depression, T inversion or a normal ECG

groups.title: AFTER the MI: what is NEW?
lines: the infarct's ARTERY predicts which complication to expect

head: h
ST-elevation MI (STEMI)
OCCLUSIVE thrombus on a ruptured plaque
REPERFUSE NOW
clue: • II, III, aVF: INFERIOR, right coronary (RCA)
inv: history + exam + ECG make the diagnosis
tx: ~no nitro if hypotensive or RV infarct
gold standard; best within 1 h of pain

head: h
Unstable angina or NSTEMI
NON-occlusive thrombus
older, multivessel disease
clue: ECG: ST DEPRESSION or T inversion
tx: • SOONER: ongoing pain, ST change, edema, low BP

head: h
Right ventricular (RV) infarction
proximal RCA: with an INFERIOR MI
tx: IV FLUIDS + PCI of the RCA

head: h
Pump failure or rupture
a LARGE or transmural MI
rupture: late presenters
clue: • > 1/3 of the left ventricle (LV) lost, anterior MI
• SOFT, apex: papillary muscle → acute mitral regurgitation (MR)
• HARSH, left sternal border: septal rupture
• free wall rupture: TAMPONADE, often fatal
inv: • septal rupture: O2 saturation STEPS UP in the RV

head: h
Arrhythmia or heart block
ventricular tachycardia (VT) or fibrillation (VF) early, scar VT days later
clue: • INFERIOR: sinus bradycardia; AV block, reversible after PCI
• ANTERIOR: Mobitz II, unstable and irreversible
inv: MOST common: accelerated idioventricular rhythm, from reperfusion
tx: then beta blocker or amiodarone; scar VT: ablation or implantable defibrillator (ICD)

head: h
Post-MI pericarditis
pleuritic pain + rub
see the PERICARDIAL DISEASE chart
clue: • LATE: Dressler syndrome, immune, weeks later

head: h
LV aneurysm or PSEUDOaneurysm
both after a LARGE transmural MI
clue: • NARROW neck, only the pericardium holds
